newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries firmer in London after overnight drop.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries firmer in London after overnight drop.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries were slightly firmer in London on Thursday, stabilising after a late selling wave in New York spilled over into Tokyo, traders said.
"The market's OK. Fundamentally nothing's changed," a trader at a U.S. investment bank said. "Wednesday's down-trade was natural. We see this as a buying opportunity."
Analysts downplayed talk that OPEC had agreed to a new quota freeze as a factor behind New York's fall, saying the selling was mainly technically driven.

The oil cartel reached a deal late on Wednesday to freeze current production quotas until the end of the year in an effort to boost world oil prices. Oil prices ticked up on the news but slipped again on Thursday.
The benchmark long bond was quoted at 98-16 at 1022 GMT, for a yield of 6.737, compared with 98-15 in Tokyo and 98-17 at Wednesday's New York close.
In New York it fell 20/32, despite a successful five-year note auction.
September T-bond futures were down 2/32 at 111-21 in automated trade.
"Yesterday's trading was strange. It's very unusual that New York's sell-off should carry across to Tokyo," said David Bloom, an economist at HSBC James Capel here.

"There's been no reason to sell further than yesterday's levels. OPEC had a knock-on effect, but the oil price is off a bit this morning. If that was the reason for the fall, I think there should be a little bit of a recovery today."
U.S. data on Thursday includes weekly jobless claims to June 21 forecast in a Reuter poll to fall to 340,000 from 347,000 the previous week, and the APICS business outlook index for June.
